To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
four antiprotozoan compounds were isolated from two Ghana-based mushroom species and their structures were established by spectroscopy and absolute configuration determination.
we have discovered two new sesterterpenoids (1, 2) and triterpenoids (3, 4) from the edible mushroom Pleurotus sp. and the medicinal mushroom Scleroderme areolatum, respectively.
we isolated two new sesterterpenoids, 1 and 2, belonging to the scalaranes and two new tricyclic triterpenes 3 and 4 from the edible mushroom P. ostreatus and the non-edible mushroom S. areolatum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of antiprotozoal metabolites from two Ghanaian fungi, P. ostreatus and S. areolatum.
a novel source of bioactive sesterterpenoids and triterpenoids from Ghanaian mushrooms.
the discovery of new natural products with antiprotozoal properties from Ghanaian mushroom species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the four new compounds (1-4) are promising candidates for further development as antimalarial and antitrypanosomal drug leads.
the four new compounds (1, 2, 3 and 4), isolated from two Ghana mushroom species, exhibited promising antiprotozoal activity against P. falciparum and T. cruzi, with no toxicity against HepG2 cells.

this study has demonstrated for the first time the isolation of scalarane sester terpenes from a terrestrial source and the isolation of new triterpenoids from the mushroom Scleroder ma areolatum, and that these compounds possess antiprotozoal activity against Plasmod ium falciparum and Trypanosoma Cruzi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the four compounds isolated from two Ghana-based mushroom species are promising candidates for further antiprotozoan drug development.

the two new scalarane-type sesterterpenoids (1 and 4) are the first of this class to be isolated from terrestrial sources, and the new 24(28)-lupane-type triterpenes 3 and 4 are the first to be isolated from a fungal source.

we isolated and characterized four new compounds from two mushroom species from Ghana, which exhibited antiprotozoal activity against the malaria parasite P. falciparum and the trypanosomatid parasite T. cruzi.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two mushroom species are potential sources of new antiprotozoal compounds, which can be further developed into lead compounds for the treatment of protozoal diseases.

the two new sesterterpenoids (1 and 4) and the two new triterpene (3 and 2) isolated from these two Ghanaian mushrooms are the first examples of their respective classes to exhibit antiplasmodial and anti-T. cruzi activities.
these new compounds are promising leads for the discovery of new antimalarial and antitrypanosomal agents from mushrooms.
